findings.title: No eligible manufacturing process under AfCFTA guidelines
findings.explanation: All production steps are operations listed in Article 7(1), such as mixing, grinding or packing. These operations alone are not eligible manufacturing processes under AfCFTA guidelines, even when the rule for heading 19.01 is met.
findings.fix: The adviser discusses with the SME if more processing in Ghana is possible.
findings.sme_action: Add processing in Ghana that is more than mixing, grinding or packing (for example cooking or drying), or discuss your plan with the adviser.

explanation.text:
Your product is likely NOT to meet the AfCFTA rules of origin.

Main reasons:
- None of the steps is an eligible manufacturing process under AfCFTA guidelines: cleaning of millet, simple grinding, simple mixing with sugar and milk powder and filling into pouches. Such steps alone do not give origin.

What to do next:
- Add processing in Ghana that is more than mixing, grinding or packing (for example cooking or drying), or discuss your plan with the adviser.
- You decide whether to apply. GRA Customs and the National AfCFTA Approval Committee make the official decision.

expected.derivation: No ingredient is in heading 19.01, so the heading-change rule is met. All steps are Art. 7(1) operations: cleaning (c), simple grinding (i), simple mixing (m), filling (k); combined (o). Art. 7(1) applies 'whether or not the requirements of Article 4 … are satisfied'.
